scope: Bounded offline review of O1/C1 final answers against their supplied full_context originals and src/english_qa.py reference_checks. No API calls; no source, prompt, answer-record, or production-code changes.
conclusion: No proven parser bug. O1 contains one real word-level quote alteration. C1 has two typographic adaptations rejected by literal matching and one editorial self-question formatted as a long direct quote. Preserve needs_review on both unchanged records; these flags are not evidence that all claims are false or that all other claims have been verified.
reason_no_code_change: The extractor pairs quotes correctly in both samples. Its advertised scope is explicit long double-quoted spans; it does not infer authorial intent. Broadening capitalization, nested-quotation punctuation, or editorial-intent matching is unnecessary for delivery and would change that contract. Never normalize actual word changes.

findings.original_span: they don't get credit for gross cash flow, they get credit for whatever net cash is left every year
findings.speaker: Warren Buffett (explicit source label)
findings.assessment: The answer changes the original grammatical subject and verb from they do not to does not; the statement is still broadly similar, but this is not an exact quotation. Checker flag is valid.
findings.repair: Restore the exact original words and adjust surrounding prose if used in a future edited answer.

findings.answer_quote: you may not be able to value it
findings.original_span: You may not be able to value it.
findings.assessment: No lexical alteration; lowercasing the first letter causes the literal-match failure. It is a formatting false positive if interpreting the flag as a substantive misquotation, but does not prove a parser defect under the exact-span contract.
findings.repair: Restore original initial capital or paraphrase without quotation marks.

findings.assessment: Words are preserved, but inner double quotation marks were changed to single quotation marks and the period to a comma. Literal comparison rejects this; no evidence of changed substantive wording.
findings.repair: Preserve the original interior punctuation using curly outer quotation marks, or paraphrase without quotation marks.

findings.answer_quote: can I say with reasonable confidence what this business's competitive position and earnings will look like far into the future?
findings.assessment: This is an editorial practical question, not a continuous span of the supplied originals. The mechanical checker intentionally cannot distinguish a proposed self-question from an attributed quote. Do not make it pass by weakening source matching.
findings.repair: Mark clearly as editorial synthesis and avoid direct-quotation formatting; source support for the broad recommendation remains a separate semantic-review issue.

verification.diagnostic: Both complete original records were rechecked offline. In-memory exact-word/typography repairs and removing quote marks from the editorial self-question produce references_checked in both, with the checker unchanged. Diagnostic strings were not saved over recorded answers.
verification.semantic_limit: Passing reference_checks only establishes citation ID resolution and matching of checked long double-quoted spans; it does not establish source support, speaker attribution, or completeness.
